compile.summary: FP32 engine built in 5.5s — 252 TRT layers, 18.9 MB.
compile.detail:
**yolo11n-pose.onnx → yolo11n-pose.fp32.plan**  ·  TensorRT 10.3.0

The engine is on disk and this is the file that gets deployed. Nothing has been run yet, so none of this is a speed measurement — the build time above is how long it took to CREATE, not how fast it goes.

**Asked for FP32, but the engine is mixed:** FP32 250 · UNKNOWN 2.

TensorRT falls back when a layer has no kernel at the precision you asked for. This is the usual reason a speed-up comes in smaller than expected — the layers that fell back are still running at the slower format.

**Layout conversion — 19% of layers**

47 of 252 layers do no maths. They only rearrange data so the next layer can read it.

Around 8% is normal at FP32. What this number is really for is comparing two builds of the SAME model: a jump after a precision change is the cost of extra shuffling, not a worse choice of kernel.

**What the engine is made of**

| Kind | Count | What it does |
|---|---:|---|
| CaskConvolution | 91 | convolutions |
| PointWiseV2 | 85 | elementwise maths, fused |
| Reformat | 47 | layout/precision conversion — overhead, not maths |
| NoOp | 13 | removed entirely |
| kgen | 5 | — |
| CaskPooling | 3 | — |
| shape_call | 2 | — |
| gemm | 2 | — |
| Resize | 2 | resizing |
| Shuffle | 1 | reshapes and transposes |
| CaskSoftMaxV2 | 1 | — |

These are TensorRT's own kernel families, after it merged what it could — which is why the count does not match the ONNX node count.

accuracy.detail:
**AP @ OKS 0.5:0.95 0.6732 against COCO-WholeBody slice (30 samples) ground truth (unchanged vs the ONNX on the same data) · 30 sample(s)**

| | |
|---|---|
| Measured against | COCO-WholeBody slice (30 samples) ground truth |
| Samples | 30 |
| Engine | `yolo11n-pose.fp32.plan` |
| Reference | `yolo11n-pose.onnx` (FP32 ONNX) |

| Metric | Engine | ONNX | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| AP @ OKS 0.5:0.95 | 0.6732 | 0.6732 | +0.0000 |
| AP @ OKS 0.5 | 0.8929 | 0.8929 | +0.0000 |
| Mean OKS | 0.7842 | 0.7842 | -0.0000 |
| PCK@0.05 | 0.5121 | 0.5121 | +0.0000 |
| People | 56 | 56 | +0.0000 |

**What these mean**

- **AP @ OKS 0.5:0.95** — COCO's pose score. OKS is IoU's analogue for poses: a per-joint Gaussian scaled by how consistently humans label that joint.
- **AP @ OKS 0.5** — The lenient threshold — poses that are broadly right.
- **Mean OKS** — Average pose similarity over every labelled person.
- **PCK@0.05** — Keypoints landing within a person-size-scaled tolerance. The readable one.
